paper.title_en: Investigation of differences between triton and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>3</mn></mmultiscripts></math> in emission dynamics and chronology via correlation functions in <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>40</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>40</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> collisions at 35 MeV/u: Insights toward resolving the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>3</mn></mmultiscripts></math> puzzle
paper.abstract_en: The <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> puzzle, namely, that <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> exhibits anomalously higher kinetic energies per nucleon than tritons (<math><mi>t</mi></math>) and <math><mi>α</mi></math> particles in the multifragmentation processes, remains a prominent open issue in the field of heavy-ion collision, as existing interpretations rely primarily on the measured energy spectra and lack constraints from multiple experimental observables. In this work, focusing on the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> puzzle in comparison to <math><mi>t</mi></math>, the differences between <math><mi>t</mi></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> in in-plane/out-of-plane emission dynamics and emission chronology from the necklike region in the midcentral <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>40</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>40</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> collisions at 35 MeV/u are experimentally investigated using the two-particle correlation functions. It is found that, compared to <math><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> shows stronger in-plane collective motion, weaker out-of-plane collective motion, and delayed emission time, collectively indicating that, compared to <math><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> tends to be emitted in a less violent collision process or the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> production is suppressed in a more violent process from an inverse perspective. This work offers novel insights into the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> puzzle by combining dynamical and chronological observables.
